canonical_claim: A 4h active-workload chaos soak at WORKERS=6 fills the disk in ~60-90 min; root cause is rustfs#3231 (upstream, open): overwriting a >128 KiB object in an un-versioned bucket leaks the previous incarnation's data directory, so every `casPut` of a `cas/refs/<...>/<shard>` body leaks one uuid dir (observed 1600+ dirs on one busy shard key; `cas/refs` reached 39 GB of a 45 GB pool vs 7.2 GB of real blob data), and the metacache walk over those dirs produces `list_merged err Io(timeout)` / `walk_dir timeout` LIST storms at ~600k files. Mitigation: WORKERS=2; durable fix is lowering ref-shard `casPut` rate (journal batching) and/or moving shard bodies under the 128 KiB inline threshold, or the upstream RustFS fix.; Merge-heavy full-scale CAS scenarios must remain below the RustFS `rustfs#3231` overwrite-churn threshold or use a fixed RustFS or fault-proxy stand; dev or reduced-round runs are the operational fallback.

evidence.notes: The RustFS issue, ref-shard key, LIST timeout text, casPut mitigation, and WORKERS=2 are present; the exact uppercase WORKERS=6 spelling is absent.
